newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt prices steady in noon trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices steady in noon trade.

text.p: Indian government security prices were largely steady in noon trade Friday, with some stocks showing a slight increase in prices, dealers said.
They said trade was limited by the prevailing call money rates and volumes will pick up once rates eased.
"Call money is above nine percent.. trade in securities will pick up only after it dips to around six percent," said a dealer.
Dealers said they expected call money to ease from current levels to around 6.0-7.0 percent on Saturday when the central bank repurchases securities for 51.5 billion rupees.
One dealer said he expected the yield on the 91-day treasury bill to come down as yields realigned, following a cut in a key central bank rate.
Yield on the 91-day treasury bill has been steady at 7.02 percent at the last two auctions. The central bank conducts its weekly auction of 91-day treasury bills later on Friday.
"The primary market yield on the 91-day treasury bill should come down slightly today to reflect changing market conditions," said a dealer.

The Reserve Bank of India on Wednesday cut the bank rate and deposit rate for deposits with maturites upto one year by one percentage point each. Banks are in turn expected to reduce deposit and lending rates in the coming days.
The expectations of a fall in interest rates sent prices of government securities shooting up on Thursday.
In latest deals on Friday, the 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 103.40 rupees, the 12.59 percent 2004 at 100.40 and the 12.14 2000 at 101.75, dealers said.
